about: Render-versus-photo checks: the structured modern record of comparisons with cited photos; earlier manual reviews can also exist in task documentation and committed render pairs. A 'cites' edge in refs/graph.json only says an author used a photo; a check says someone rendered the game from that photo's camera (scripts/shoot_views.cjs --task=<id> --as=after) and compared the two. Each check: task (data/build_queue.json id), feature (evidence-graph feature id), photo, render (committed after-render, usually docs/reviews/<task>/<photo>-after.png), before (optional), checked (date), by, result matches | differs | not-comparable, notes, and for differs a followUp task id that is not done. A photo used for a check needs a reviewed looksAt in data/reference_tags.json so the render faces the photo's subject. build_references.py --check fails when a done task has a photo without a check, unless the task is in legacyUnchecked; that list may only shrink.

From the lane at the east portal: before, a plain three-column-tile lane ran into the walkway with no level change; after, three white-nosed risers with plain terracotta treads climb on the left, the red studded ramp fills the right, the offset terracotta floor with blue-and-white inserts, the pebble mat, the round west arch, the two brown double doors and the white wall kerbs all appear in the photo order (steps, ramp, floor, mat, doors, arch). Tread depth, rise and mat position are estimates; the photo shows more stepped impost at the arch and a darker, glossier floor. Camera hand-set in the walkway frame (unsolved starting pose), so composition is comparable but not pixel-aligned.
